div.p: Pound 5 Holland Place, Chambers London W8
Cable Quinn confirm or remit you telegraphically nothing here remitting

div.note: Official notations on this telegram indicate that JJ sent it to Pound from Zurich on 20 August 1917 at 11 a.m. These data agree with a follow-up letter that JJ wrote Pound the same day (SL 226-27). The English office stamp and additional notations indicate that the telegram was received in London on 22 August at 7 a.m. Pound replied to JJ the next day, 23 August, by cable and by separate letter (Pound/Joyce 124-25).

note.p: On 23 August 1917, Pound wrote JJ to say that he was baffled by this cabled message and added that he had cabled JJ back: “WHAT do you want cash[?]” (Pound/Joyce 124-25). The New York lawyer John Quinn (1870-1924), a collector of modern art and literary manuscripts, had arranged to purchase items from JJ, including the manuscript of his play Exiles. Pound had written JJ on 17 July 1917 that Quinn had sent “an advance” on the Exiles manuscript (Pound/Joyce 121). JJ was still eagerly awaiting that payment (“nothing here”) and wanted Quinn to cable the cash to Pound’s care (“confirm or remit you telegraphically”). JJ explained the cable in a letter to Pound dated the same day, 20 August, and also described the “violent Hexenschuss” (lumbago) that had attacked him while he was walking in Zurich on 18 August and then a resurgence of glaucoma the following day (SL 226-27). A few days later, JJ was to undergo surgery for an iridectomy at the Zurich Augenklinik (Ellmann, JJ 417). For JJ’s belief that his eye problems were connected to rheumatism, see JJ to Pound,19 July 1915, notes; 10 March 1916, notes.

Later, when Quinn finally received acts two and three of Exiles, he sent JJ, on 18 August 1917, a “Zurich draft for 522.50 francs, being the equivalent of £25,” which did not reach JJ until mid-September (Myron Schwartzman, “‘Quinnigan’s Quake!’ John Quinn’s Letters to James Joyce, 1916-1920,” Bulletin of Research in the Humanities, vol. 81, no. 2 [Summer 1978]: 231).
